ApiLoginRequest.description:
Credentials for `POST /api/auth/login`.

`device_name` names the token so it can be rotated and revoked per device
("Pixel 8", "iPad"). It is attacker-controlled text that ends up in a token
label, so it is length-capped and never interpolated anywhere but the label.

`code` carries the TOTP or recovery code and is required only when the
account has confirmed two-factor authentication — enforced in the controller,
because demanding it up front would leak which accounts have 2FA enabled.
ApiLoginRequest.title: ApiLoginRequest

CampaignAdFormat.description: Meta Ads placement/format. `LeadForm` targets Meta's native Instant Forms — the single highest-intent lead-gen unit on Meta — and is the format the generation agent leans on when `business_goal` is Leads.
CampaignAdFormat.title: CampaignAdFormat

CampaignBusinessGoal.description: Campaigns is a paid Meta Ads module — every goal here is acquisition or retention-oriented, unlike SocialMedia's organic set (which also allows 'viral'/'community'). Own Domain enum copy — modules never cross-import.
CampaignBusinessGoal.title: CampaignBusinessGoal

CampaignFunnelStage.description: TOFU/MOFU/BOFU/LOYALTY classification the topic-ideation agent assigns to every candidate Meta Ads angle. Drives which CTA and Meta objective rules the generation agent applies — Loyalty is the 4th stage (retention/ retargeting) real Meta Ads accounts budget separately from acquisition, per 2026 full-funnel playbooks (60-70% TOFU / 20-30% MOFU / 5-10% BOFU / 5-10% Loyalty budget split).
CampaignFunnelStage.title: CampaignFunnelStage

CampaignLanguage.description: Output language the user picks for AI generation — never inferred, always explicit (the same niche can be worked in either market). pt-PT = European Portuguese (Portugal), not Brazilian.
CampaignLanguage.title: CampaignLanguage

CampaignPlatform.description: Meta Ads surface the campaign targets. 'Both' generates adapted copy for Facebook AND Instagram in one attempt (see PlatformCampaignContentData) — a single angle rarely needs a 3rd Meta surface, unlike SocialMedia's 5-network spread, so this stays a flat enum rather than a multi-select.
CampaignPlatform.title: CampaignPlatform

ContentLanguage.description: Output language the user picks for AI generation — never inferred, always explicit (the same topic/niche can be worked in either market). pt-PT = European Portuguese (Portugal), not Brazilian.
ContentLanguage.title: ContentLanguage

FunnelStage.description: TOFU/MOFU/BOFU classification the topic-ideation agent assigns to every candidate topic. Drives which CTA rules the content-generation agent applies — it is not cosmetic: TOFU never gets a hard-sell CTA, BOFU never gets a soft "follow for more".
FunnelStage.title: FunnelStage

GenerateCampaignData.description:
Input for Step 2 (quality-loop campaign generation). One instance is
reused across every iteration of the Infrastructure quality-loop Job;
only the previous-scores/weaknesses feedback (passed separately to the
port) changes between iterations.
GenerateCampaignData.title: GenerateCampaignData

GenerateContentVariantData.description:
Shared input for the social-copy and reel-package generators — both need
only the chosen topic/angle/trend (from {@see PostTopicIdeaData} or a
freehand topic) plus the provider, same as {@see GeneratePostContentData}
minus the cover-image flag.
GenerateContentVariantData.title: GenerateContentVariantData

GeneratePostContentData.description:
Input for full draft generation: either a title picked from
{@see PostTopicIdeaData} or a freehand topic the user typed directly.

`imageMode` decides how much cover artwork is actually rendered against the
brand palette — `full` composites background + subject + title, `base`
renders only the palette background plate for the user to composite on, and
`none` bills no image call. The layered prompts come back in all three
cases, so `none` still leaves the user able to generate externally.
GeneratePostContentData.title: GeneratePostContentData

GenerateSocialMediaContentData.description:
Input for Step 2 (quality-loop content generation). One instance is reused
across every iteration of {@see GenerateSocialMediaContentJob};
only the previous-scores/weaknesses feedback (passed separately to the
port) changes between iterations.

`imageMode` decides how much artwork is actually rendered against the theme
palette — `full` (composite cover + 5 platform graphics), `base` (palette
background plates only, to composite elsewhere) or `none` (prompts only, no
billed image call). It defaults to `full` so an omitted field keeps the
previous behaviour.
GenerateSocialMediaContentData.title: GenerateSocialMediaContentData

PostImageMode.description:
How much of the cover artwork the AI assist step should actually render. All three modes always return the layered BrandPalette prompts, so the user can regenerate externally regardless of the choice — the mode only decides whether a billed image call is made, and what it draws. | | |---| | `full`
Composite cover: palette background + subject + short title. | | `base`
Palette-locked background plate only — no subject, no title. | | `none`
No image call at all; prompts only. |
PostImageMode.title: PostImageMode

SocialMediaImageMode.description:
How much of the cover / per-platform artwork the generation loop actually renders. Same three-way contract as Post's {@see PostImageMode}, extended to the 5-platform fan-out: one choice applies to the cover AND every platform variant, because mixing modes per platform buys nothing and doubles the billing surface. All three modes always return the palette-locked prompts on the DTO, so the user can render externally regardless of the choice — the mode only decides whether a billed image call is made, and what it draws. `Full` is expensive: 6 images (cover + 5 platforms) per accepted attempt. `Base` renders the palette background plate only — the plate a designer composites a title over in Figma/Canva. `None` bills nothing. | | |---| | `full`
Composite: palette background + subject + short title (route A/B/C). | | `base`
Palette-locked background plate only — no subject, no title. | | `none`
No image call at all; prompts only. |
SocialMediaImageMode.title: SocialMediaImageMode

StorePublicContactSupportRequest.description:
The public landing-page contact form. Unauthenticated: the route is throttled
and honeypot-protected ({@see ProtectAgainstSpam}), and this
request is the authoritative validation gate — the client-side Zod schema is
UX only (OWASP §3 / §15.5). Triage columns (`readed`, `is_spam`, `spam_*`)
are NOT accepted here; the submission pipeline owns them.
StorePublicContactSupportRequest.title: StorePublicContactSupportRequest

SuggestCampaignTopicsData.description:
Input for Step 1 (10 Meta Ads lead-gen angle candidates). `niche` is an
optional steer — when blank the agent leans entirely on the company
profile + Tavily trend research, mirroring
{@see SuggestSocialMediaTopicsData}.
SuggestCampaignTopicsData.title: SuggestCampaignTopicsData

SuggestPostTopicsData.description:
Input for topic ideation. The flow is category-first: the chosen blog
category IS the niche, so `categoryUuid` is required and its name +
description drive both the Tavily research queries and the agent prompt.
`topic` stays an optional extra steer that narrows the angle inside that
category — when blank the agent scans the whole category.
SuggestPostTopicsData.title: SuggestPostTopicsData

SuggestSocialMediaTopicsData.description:
Input for Step 1 (10 viral topics). `niche` is an optional steer — when
blank the agent leans entirely on the company profile + Tavily trend
research, mirroring {@see SuggestPostTopicsData}.
SuggestSocialMediaTopicsData.title: SuggestSocialMediaTopicsData
